# saturating-time Windows clock granularity patch

Based on the published `saturating-time` 0.5.0 crate, upstream
<https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/arti>, commit
`ce8bc6e0998bd5a4efdf06dd62dce53c98ea1087` (Arti 2.7.0).
The registry archive SHA-256 is
`a586db154f85f3faf78398c37b6792d71f99d2253d3277571e14f8a8c6e49a65`.
The published source, normalized manifest, original manifest and commit
provenance are retained. The MIT and Apache license files come from the same
upstream release tag. Its unused package lockfile is omitted; the application's
root lockfile resolves dependencies.

Arti 0.47 requires `saturating-time` 0.5. The previous EpixNet fork, version
0.4.1 at `afd652ed569053f878c30f6b0ef44528cd900d46`, cannot satisfy that
requirement. Published 0.5.0 still contains the Windows bootstrap hang that
the fork fixed.

The platform-limit search assumes every positive duration either changes the
time or overflows. Windows `SystemTime` uses 100ns FILETIME ticks. A smaller
duration rounds to zero and returns the same time. Upstream keeps retrying
that unchanged value forever when Arti first uses saturating time arithmetic.

This patch carries forward the existing non-progress fix:

- Add `PartialEq` to the internal sealed trait.
- Treat `Some(unchanged)` like an exhausted step: halve the step, or finish
  when it reaches 1ns.
- Keep the upstream 0.5 `web-time-compat` dependency and `InstantExt::get()`.
- Use portable durations in documentation examples and keep tests requiring
  nanosecond `SystemTime` precision on Unix.

Two synthetic 100ns-clock tests exercise the production `find_limit` function
for both bounds. They require the exact representable limit and observed
rounded steps. A 512-call guard makes the original infinite loop fail promptly
on every host. A Windows-only public-API test verifies real FILETIME limits
and saturating arithmetic.

Run the crate tests with:

```sh
cargo test --manifest-path vendor/saturating-time/Cargo.toml
```

Run the same command in a bounded Windows CI job to cover the real platform
representation. The synthetic tests reproduce the bug on Linux too. Remove
the standalone vendor lockfile generated by this command after testing.

Remove this patch only after adopting an upstream release that handles
non-progressing clock operations, with both the coarse-clock regressions and
real Windows limit checks passing. Do not simply remove the patch when
upgrading Arti: that would restore the Windows bootstrap hang.
